c813fd2bc859cb5fa88341f68769b6ced88b959f.summary: A Substack blog post by Natto Team, titled Part One of a piece on Russian extortion operations and hybrid warfare. It was published 2024-05-01 and archived 2026-11-25. The excerpt holds only quotes: Vladimir Putin's 2017 remarks and hacker Pavel Sitnikov's 2020 interview on state-aligned hacking, plus a truncated question about CL0P ransomware and U.S. critical infrastructure. The post is paywalled after the excerpt, so no findings, techniques or attributions appear in this text.

c87961c73eb96062c14d4b93e03dc45bd6b7cebd.summary: Symantec (Broadcom) protection bulletin on SteganoAmor, a campaign the bulletin attributes to threat group TA558. Per the bulletin, the campaign hides malicious code inside image files (steganography) and still uses the 2017 Microsoft Office Equation Editor flaw CVE-2017-11882. The group is said to target tourism and hospitality, with extensive focus on Latin America. Delivered payloads may include Remcos, Agent Tesla, Formbook, Guloader, Lokibot and Xworm.

c8b149a5adf91abf6ea383657c5ee1906438f85f.summary: Report on a group it calls Space Pirates, described as a previously unknown Chinese hacking group that targets Russian aerospace and related organisations with phishing emails and custom malware. The report says the group is believed to have started in 2017 and has links to other known groups, which it treats as tentative. Victims are described in Russia, Georgia and Mongolia, including Russian companies with state participation. Tools named include PlugX, ShadowPad, Deed RAT, BH_A006 and MyKLoadClient. The page ends with an unrelated whitepaper advert.
